# Getting `input()` from a user

In lots of programs you write, you will want to get a user to give data to your program.


## Exercise - Getting User `input()`

We will now do another exercise! [Deeper data validation, using statements, comparisons, API calls etc. some ideas are below]

*Remember*: your [assignments, tests and exams](https://pxr687.github.io/Intro_Comp_Programming/1_02_Class_Grades_Assignments_Exams.html) will also be a bit like this.

Click [here 🚀](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/pxr687/Intro_Comp_Programming/main?urlpath=tree/exercise_4b_input.ipynb) to launch the exercise on Binder.

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML
import numpy as np

roll = np.random.randint(1, 7)

message_text = f"""
<h2 style="color: green;">
🎲 The dice rolled a {roll}!
</h2>
"""

display(HTML(message_text))
```

```{python}
import webbrowser
import tempfile

roll = np.random.randint(1, 7)

bet = input('Make your bet!:')

if roll == bet:
    emoji = ":)"
else:
    emoji = ":("

message_text = f"""
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
<h1 style="color: green;">
🎲 Dice Roll
</h1>
<p style="color: red;">
The dice rolled a {roll}.
</p>
<p style="color: green;">
You bet it would roll {bet}.
Your bet is {bet == roll} {emoji}
</p>
</body>
</html>
"""

display(HTML(message_text))
```
